bill.title: Summer Meals REACH Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.
bill.officialSummary: Summer Meals Reaching Every Area's Child Hunger Act of 2025 or the Summer Meals REACH Act of 2025 This bill permanently makes all children eligible to participate in the Summer Food Service Program. This includes requiring reimbursement to camps for meals served to all children. This Department of Agriculture program provides free meals to children in low-income areas through eligible organizations, primarily when school is not in session. Specifically, the bill extends certain program modifications, which generally expanded the program and were authorized and implemented to respond to COVID-19. For example, the bill permanently authorizes non-congregate meal distribution, which is meal distribution outside of the typically required group, or congregate, setting (e.g., grab-and-go meal service). Further, the bill expands eligible service institutions by permanently allowing for on-site or off-site (i.e., remote) food service monitoring.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would permanently expand the Summer Food Service Program, which provides free meals to children when school is not in session. It would make all children eligible to participate (not just those in low-income areas), require reimbursement for meals served at camps, and allow flexible meal distribution such as grab-and-go service and remote monitoring of food providers. These changes were originally implemented temporarily during COVID-19 and would now become permanent.

industries.rationale: The bill expands a federal food distribution program, increasing demand for food suppliers and processors who provide meals to participating organizations.
Restaurant chains and food service operators that run camps or serve as eligible organizations would receive expanded reimbursement for meals served to all children.
Schools and educational organizations that operate summer programs would be affected by the expanded eligibility and new service delivery options.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill permanently would make all children eligible to participate in the Summer Food Service Program.
plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in farming, and food prices. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
